result.title: A Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Official Statistics
result.summary: Official statistics are critical datasets for a wide variety of actors, including policymakers and businesses. For providers of official statistics, improving accessibility, governance, and disclosure of their data is of key importance. This can be improved by providing question-answering systems based on text-to-SQL approaches. However, existing text-to-SQL benchmarks do not resemble this setting. Official statistics are published as open-domain catalogs of thousands of wide tables whose columns and values are codes, and whose meaning is recorded in separate metadata rather than in a relational schema. To address this gap, we introduce LOCuST, a text-to-SQL benchmark that pairs over two thousand English and Dutch tables from Statistics Netherlands with a semantic knowledge graph. The graph describes the tables, measures, and dimension codes through labels, definitions, hierarchies, and units, and is the external knowledge a system needs to find the right tables and ground a question in the right codes. The benchmark includes expert-annotated questions for different query and aggregation types, including raw value retrieval, summations, proportion calculations, and joins. Alongside standard evaluation measures, we introduce an observation F1 metric that measures how close a query is to the ground truth even when the answers are different. We evaluate a variety of state-of-the-art LLMs and find that they struggle to write SQL that answers the questions correctly.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 LOCuST 基准：把荷兰统计局两千余张英/荷语宽表与描述表、度量及维度代码的语义知识图谱配对，提供专家标注的多类型查询与聚合问题，并在常规指标外引入 observation F1，评测显示当前 LLM 写出的 SQL 仍难以正确回答问题。
AI.relevance_reason: 「从数千张宽表中定位正确表、再借外部元数据把问题落到正确代码」的证据筛选设定，以及答案不同仍可部分计分的 observation F1，可能为 LVR 的视觉证据定位与中间状态评价提供类比线索，可供核查。
